title: Filters and blend modes (intro)
learningObjectives: Explain filters and blend modes (intro) and use the relevant CSS properties appropriately.

understand.concept: CSS filter functions apply visual effects such as blur(), brightness(), contrast(), grayscale(), and drop-shadow(). mix-blend-mode controls how an element's content blends with its backdrop; background-blend-mode controls blending among background layers.
understand.whyItMatters: Filters can affect rendering cost and readability. Blend modes depend on the backdrop and stacking context, so test them against the actual page background and provide a sensible fallback appearance.
understand.analogy: A filter is like applying a visual lens; a blend mode describes how two layers combine where they overlap.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy helps visualise the effect; CSS rendering and stacking follow browser layout and painting rules.

explain.narrative: The label receives a drop shadow and blends with the gradient backdrop. Change screen to normal and compare.

practise.guidedTask: Create a small visual tile using grayscale() and contrast(). Then test one blend mode against two different backdrops.
practise.independentTask: Build a small component that uses this visual treatment without reducing readability or keyboard usability.
hints: Inspect the rendered result against different backgrounds.
Change one property at a time.
Keep focus indicators visible and content readable.

questions.prompt: Which CSS property controls how an element blends with its backdrop?
questions.explanation: mix-blend-mode controls the blending of an element's content with its backdrop.

questions.prompt: What should you verify when adding decorative visual effects?
options: Only whether the effect looks fashionable
Whether the effect hides focus outlines
questions.explanation: Visual effects should not make content or interactive states harder to perceive.
